text:
Paloma Rivera: heads up — running into a flaky case with the Python SDK async stream. I cancel the consumer task on shutdown but sometimes more chunks arrive after cancel.

Kai Chen: hmm. Is this using httpx SSE or chunked transfer? can you paste a minimal snippet?

Paloma Rivera: httpx chunked. Minimal:```py
async def stream(prompt):
    async with client.stream('/v1/streams', json={'prompt': prompt}) as resp:
        async for line in resp.aiter_lines():
            yield parse(line)
```
On SIGINT we cancel the task and call `await client.close()` — most times it stops immediately, but a few times ~1-3 extra chunks trickle in.

Mike L.: sounds like a race between task.cancel() and the generator finalizer or httpx background worker. do you call `agen.aclose()` anywhere?

Paloma Rivera: not in the cancel path. I rely on `await client.close()` to close sockets. Tried adding `finally: await resp.aclose()` in the wrapper but still saw late chunks occasionally.

sara: httpx connection pooling can be surprising — sockets may be returned to pool and background tasks can flush pending data. Also a partial line in the buffer could be yielded after close if aiter_lines() splits on newlines.

Kai Chen: internal memory: we had a bug where the async generator finalizer re-entered because aclose wasn't idempotent and weakref finalizers reopened the stream. Could be the generator's finalizer awaiting something that reschedules I/O.

Mike L.: one mitigation is to make `aclose()` synchronous from the public API (i.e., set an _closed flag synchronously then await cleanup) so users see the stream as closed immediately. Also dedupe terminal events so duplicate final chunks aren't emitted.

Paloma Rivera: quick local test: changed cancel sequence to `await agen.aclose()` before task.cancel() — that prevented resumes locally. Cloud repro still flaky but much less common.

dev-bot: Created issue #2785: "py-sdk: async generator resumes after cancel (finalizer race)" — assigned to Kai.

Kai Chen: I'll take #2785. Plan: add an _is_closed guard in the generator wrapper, make aclose idempotent, and add unit test that cancels mid-iteration asserting no further chunks. Also update docs on shutdown.

Paloma Rivera: will attach logs + request ids to the issue. I also noticed duplicate final chunks when canceling right as server sent terminal chunk — looks like both server close and our finalizer emit the terminal event.

Mike L.: we'll add terminal dedupe (track emission of terminal event per stream id). Also update typing docs to emphasize `agen.aclose()` for graceful shutdown.

sara: small DX request: can we add a Quickstart note and FAQ item about async stream shutdown? A one-liner showing `try/except KeyboardInterrupt: await agen.aclose()` would save folks. People assume task.cancel is enough.

Kai Chen: good call. I'll include a short snippet in the SDK quickstart and link to the issue. Paloma, if you can add a CI flake test that cancels at random timing and asserts no more chunks, that’ll help catch regressions.

Paloma Rivera: adding the flaky repro test now and attaching salt logs. Thanks everyone — `await agen.aclose()` is a workable mitigation for me for now. Will update #2785 with CI results. :thumbsup:

Mike L.: prototype PR up that gates finalizer emission and marks streams closed immediately (not landing yet). leaving review comments on #2785.

Kai Chen: moving the issue to in-progress. Will ping when PR is ready for review.

sara: created docs PR with shutdown snippet and linked to the quickstart.

Paloma Rivera: confirmed in CI forcing `agen.aclose()` removed the resume in all runs. Cloud still had one noisy case but cannot repro locally. Thanks all!"
